_meta.title: TRIZ 40 Inventive Principles
_meta.note: Canonical numbering with concise English paraphrases. Look up numbers deterministically; translate each principle into a causal mechanism for the problem at hand.

principles.name: Segmentation
principles.classic: Divide an object into independent parts; make it sectional or modular.

principles.name: Taking out / Extraction
principles.classic: Separate an interfering part or isolate the only needed part.

principles.name: Local quality
principles.classic: Make each part fulfill a different, locally optimal function.

principles.name: Asymmetry
principles.classic: Replace symmetric forms with asymmetric ones.

principles.name: Merging / Consolidation
principles.classic: Bring identical or adjacent operations together in space or time.

principles.name: Universality
principles.classic: Make an object perform multiple functions and eliminate other parts.

principles.name: Nested doll / Nesting
principles.classic: Place one object inside another; use layered containment.

principles.name: Anti-weight / Counterweight
principles.classic: Compensate an object's weight by coupling it to a lifting force.

principles.name: Preliminary anti-action
principles.classic: Preload an opposing action before a harmful one occurs.

principles.name: Preliminary action / Prior action
principles.classic: Perform a required change fully or partly in advance.

principles.name: Beforehand cushioning
principles.classic: Prepare emergency means beforehand to offset low reliability.

principles.name: Equipotentiality
principles.classic: Remove the need to raise or lower in a potential field.

principles.name: The other way round / Inversion
principles.classic: Invert the action; make movable parts fixed and fixed parts movable.

principles.name: Spheroidality / Curvature
principles.classic: Use curves or rollers instead of straight lines or planes.

principles.name: Dynamics
principles.classic: Allow characteristics to change so they are optimal at each stage.

principles.name: Partial or excessive action
principles.classic: If the full action is difficult, do slightly less or slightly more.

principles.name: Another dimension
principles.classic: Move into another dimension, tilt the object, or use multi-level arrangements.

principles.name: Mechanical vibration / Oscillation
principles.classic: Oscillate or increase the frequency of an action.

principles.name: Periodic action
principles.classic: Replace continuous action with periodic or pulsed action.

principles.name: Continuity of useful action
principles.classic: Work continuously and remove idle intervals.

principles.name: Skipping / Rushing through
principles.classic: Conduct a harmful or hazardous operation at very high speed.

principles.name: Blessing in disguise / Turn harm into benefit
principles.classic: Use a harmful factor to achieve a positive effect.

principles.name: Feedback
principles.classic: Introduce feedback, or change the magnitude and influence of existing feedback.

principles.name: Intermediary / Mediator
principles.classic: Use an intermediary carrier or process, temporarily or permanently.

principles.name: Self-service
principles.classic: Make an object serve or repair itself and use waste resources.

principles.name: Copying
principles.classic: Use inexpensive copies instead of an unavailable, expensive, or fragile original.

principles.name: Cheap short-living objects
principles.classic: Replace an expensive durable object with inexpensive short-lived ones.

principles.name: Mechanics substitution
principles.classic: Replace a mechanical means with a field, sensory, or other interaction.

principles.name: Pneumatics and hydraulics
principles.classic: Use gas or liquid parts instead of solid parts.

principles.name: Flexible shells and thin films
principles.classic: Use flexible shells, thin films, or isolating membranes.

principles.name: Porous materials
principles.classic: Make an object porous or add porous elements.

principles.name: Color changes
principles.classic: Change the color or transparency of an object or its environment.

principles.name: Homogeneity
principles.classic: Make interacting objects of the same material or compatible behavior.

principles.name: Discarding and recovering
principles.classic: Discard or modify used parts and restore consumables during operation.

principles.name: Parameter changes
principles.classic: Change physical state, concentration, flexibility, temperature, or another parameter.

principles.name: Phase transitions
principles.classic: Use phenomena accompanying phase transitions.

principles.name: Thermal expansion
principles.classic: Use thermal expansion or contraction of materials.

principles.name: Strong oxidants / Boosted interactions
principles.classic: Replace a normal medium with an enriched or activated one to intensify interaction.

principles.name: Inert atmosphere
principles.classic: Replace a normal environment with an inert one.

principles.name: Composite materials
principles.classic: Replace homogeneous materials with composite or multi-property ones.
